findings.title: Plain Error instead of TRPCError for auth failure
findings.body: Throwing a generic Error yields an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR response and gets logged as a server fault. A missing or foreign credential should throw TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN so clients and monitoring get correct semantics.

findings.title: Cache actions shown only for GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE; delegation cache delete impossible
findings.body: hasCache requires integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE and a truthy cacheUpdatedAt. For delegation credentials (negative or in-memory ids) the cache is keyed by user rather than credentialId. The status lookup and deleteCache (which looks up the credential in the DB) will not work for them. Also, `hasCache` is typed Date|null|false|undefined, and the date passes through tRPC serialization.

findings.title: Pointless updateMany with empty data on every cache refresh
findings.body: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) runs after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache. With empty data, Prisma's @updatedAt may still bump the timestamps, but the intent is unclear. It adds a write per webhook and the value is never displayed, since the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt. The PR notes even admit this is unneeded. It should be removed.

findings.title: Upsert update does not reliably bump updatedAt
findings.body: The cache status shows the max updatedAt of CalendarCache rows, which depends on the upsert update touching the row. Prisma's @updatedAt is set automatically on update, so this works. However, the migration's DEFAULT NOW() makes all existing rows appear 'just updated' at deploy time, so the displayed last-updated time is misleading for legacy rows.

findings.title: macOS-only sed -i '' and unrelated dev script
findings.body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux sed, where it treats '' as the file name. The relative ENV_FILE path depends on cwd. The script is also unrelated to this feature and slipped into the PR.
